paragraphs: Worcestershire County Council's own service, Worcestershire Fostering, recruits carers for children in the county's care, alongside independent agencies such as those listed on this page. It offers short-term, long-term, respite, buddy and parent and child fostering, the Valuing Care scheme for children moving on from residential homes, and family and friends care.

To apply you need to be 21 or older, have a spare room for a child over two, good spoken and written English, financial stability, time for the assessment, training and social worker visits, and no criminal offences relating to children.

The council's payment page, correct from 1 April 2025, combines an age-based child allowance with a skills payment of £110, £160 or £220 a week depending on level. Totals run from £286 a week for a baby at level 1 to £487 a week for a 16 or 17-year-old at level 3, plus expenses such as mileage, clothing and school uniform grants. It also lists retainer payments between placements, up to four weeks of respite a year, 24/7 emergency support and half-price leisure passes.

New carers complete Skills to Foster over four sessions (about 20 hours), then core training refreshed every three years. Ask the council and two or three of the agencies below what they offer, and compare the support as well as the pay.
